items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: I worked with Slam for a while, and Slam drank quite a bit, and so did Beryl Barrel, and it got to the point that I had to almost transport the group, you know, and see that they got to work.

ctx.x: That particular time I only played Paris, you know, and we would go -- just for say about three weeks. Paris was beautiful then too, you know, this wide open, just lovely. But my next trip to Europe was with Nat

Cole. I'd made many trips over there with him, though. We toured the whole -- we did the whole bit. But any way coming to Nat Cole, now, this is something else. I -- now, I won't go to Nat yet, I'll wait. I worked with Slam for a while, and Slam drank quite a bit, and so did Beryl Barrel, and it got to the point that I had to almost transport the group, you know, and see that they got to work. And I never liked that role, that wasn't my role.

And one night I just -- after the engagement I just packed up and left, couldn't stand it any longer. And I went to New York and I just decided to lay off for a while. I wouldn't play at all, I just -- not professionally. You know, I wouldn't accept any engagements. I just wanted to kind of regroup, get my thoughts together, and see what was happening with me.
